newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow awaits details on NATO-Russia force.
newsitem.headline: Moscow awaits details on NATO-Russia force.

text.p: Moscow declined comment on Wednesday on a U.S. proposal to create a permanent Russia-NATO force but hoped Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would explain the idea during talks in Moscow this week.
Albright proposed to alliance foreign ministers in Brussels on Tuesday that a brigade should be modelled on NATO-Russian cooperation in the Bosnia peace force.

It would also be part of measures to assure Russia of NATO's peaceful intentions when it goes ahead with a plan to invite some countries of central and eastern Europe to join the Western defence alliance.
Moscow opposes the plan and says it will undermine its security and weaken President Boris Yeltsin's government.
Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov declined comment on Albright's proposal.

"I have not heard about it form her (Albright)," he told Reuters after a news conference following talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat. "I heard about it through the press, so I will refrain from any comment."

Deputy Foreign Minister Nikolai Afanasyevsky told Interfax news agency that Moscow hoped Albright would discuss the proposal in talks with Russian leaders, including President Boris Yeltsin, on Thursday and Friday.
"This would be of interest to us," he said.

The proposal for a brigade, primarily to be a peace-keeping force, would complement the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's vision of a joint alliance-Russia body that would promote regular dialogue on security issues.
But Albright declined to give details, saying the idea was in its infancy.
